item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Multiscale modelling of biochemical networks for bioinspired computing and temporal memory (ROMA "Tor Vergata")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-10-26 23:59
Institution: ROMA "Tor Vergata", Roma
Field: Physics / 02/PHYS-06 Fisica per le scienze della vita, l'ambiente e i beni culturali, didattica e storia della fisica

Modelling of biochemical networks for bioinspired computing. Deterministic and stochastic kinetic models and compartmental reaction-diffusion models will be implemented to study how molecular exchange, relaxation times and noise affect temporal memory and responses to stimulus sequences. Activities include numerical verification through conservation tests, analytical limits and convergence; sensitivity, identifiability and uncertainty-propagation analyses; comparison with passive, uncoupled and well-mixed controls; and assessment of predictions under conditions withheld from calibration. Outputs will include reproducible code, benchmarks and a report on model validity domains, supporting…

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Investigation of combined, non-invasive multimodal therapies targeting glioblastoma in cellular and in vivo models (ROMA "Tor Vergata")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-10-26 23:59
Institution: ROMA "Tor Vergata", Roma, Rm
Field: Physics / 02/PHYS-06 Fisica per le scienze della vita, l'ambiente e i beni culturali, didattica e storia della fisica

The project aims to develop and validate multimodal, non-invasive therapeutic strategies for the treatment of glioblastoma, through the integration of Focused Ultrasound (FUS) and innovative therapeutic agents. In particular, the ability of FUS to promote the localized release and intratumoral accumulation of the therapeutic agents will be evaluated. To this end, treatment planning systems for FUS and microbubble cavitation monitoring systems will be developed and validated, so as to ensure safe and effective control of the treatment. item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Dynamics of Diversity in Complex Systems: Entropy, Extinction and Innovation (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-09 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Physics / 02/PHYS-04 Fisica teorica della materia, modelli, metodi matematici e applicazioni

The research activity will focus on the study of diversity in complex systems described by discrete or continuous probability distributions undergoing time evolution. It will analyze the conditions determining the conservation, reduction, or irreversible loss of diversity, with particular attention to the role of entropy, distribution support, statistical divergences, rare events, and extinction times. The project will leverage tools from statistical mechanics, information theory, stochastic processes, population dynamics, and neural networks. Within this framework, machine learning systems and artificial generative models will also be considered, where iterative generation and learning…

item.description:

Institution: Univ. PALERMO, Palermo
Field: Physics / 02/PHYS-03 Fisica sperimentale della materia e applicazioni

The beneficiary will carry out research activities aimed at developing microsensors based on the coupling of photoluminescent nanomaterials with optical Whispering Gallery Mode (WGM) microresonators, such as dielectric microspheres made of polystyrene and glass. The goal is to develop active microresonators whose emission can be engineered through coupling to the photonic modes of the microresonator.

GERAS project aims to create an innovative, non-invasive technological ecosystem for the prevention and monitoring of biological aging, which currently represents one of the crucial challenges for public health. The underlying idea of the project is to integrate smart hardware devices (smart rings, interactive mirrors, kiosks) with software platforms and modules based on advanced technologies (body tracking markerless, applied gaming) and Artificial Intelligence and Explainable Artificial Intelligence models. FRAMEGLOW aims to develop an advanced fracture-mechanics theory and apply it to understanding how climate change weakens snow and ice.
